evidence.detail: HEAD and the launcher target both resolve to c4cb4d28f9b710e4f24366ec6fbb61e810246d96; the working tree is clean and detached at that commit.
The base-to-target diff changes six allowed files: the workflow, README.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, and ISSUE-0014 governance records. No product source or dependency manifest changed.

The workflow SHA-pins actions/setup-node, selects Node 22, enables npm caching from frontend/package-lock.json, and runs npm ci, npm run build, and npm test in frontend/ after the existing Python checks.
README.md and CONTRIBUTING.md now describe frontend build and test coverage in CI.
Governance validation could not execute to completion because the read-only review environment provides no writable temporary directory; it raised FileNotFoundError before producing a result.
The backend suite ran 188 tests but failed with 76 errors because the review sandbox prohibits loopback socket binding; affected tests raised PermissionError in ThreadingHTTPServer.bind().

frontend/node_modules is absent. The read-only, network-restricted review environment cannot run npm ci or create the build output, so the frontend build, positive test run, and negative-test proof could not be independently reproduced.

evidence: Expected: project/status/CURRENT.md must be an internally consistent current-state index naming the current gate and next permitted action.

Observed: line 207 says ISSUE-0014 is start-authorized and awaiting review, while line 213 says it is PLANNED/not started, line 222 says deciding whether to start it remains open, and line 223 says CI still omits the frontend and ISSUE-0014 is not started.
The same candidate adds DECISION-030 and changes the workflow to run the frontend checks, so the contradictory statements are stale at the reviewed SHA.
findings.remediation: Update the current-state table so the milestone, blockers, and tracked-follow-up rows consistently state that ISSUE-0014 is implemented and under round-0 review, and that the candidate workflow now contains the frontend CI steps. Keep any hosted-runner/YAML execution limitation explicit.
findings.title: Current-state index contradicts the candidate’s issue and CI status
findings.verification: At the repaired commit, search project/status/CURRENT.md for ISSUE-0014, “not started,” and “CI still does not run”; confirm every current-state statement agrees with the active ISSUE_REVIEW gate and the workflow diff, then rerun governance validation.

limitations: The mandatory governance check could not complete because no writable temporary directory is available.
The backend suite could not pass because sandbox policy blocks its loopback socket tests; 76 of 188 tests errored for that environmental reason.
The frontend build and tests could not be independently executed because dependencies are absent and the environment is read-only and network-restricted.
The recorded positive and negative frontend results in project/issues/ISSUE-0014.md are author-provided summaries rather than independently reproducible raw output in this checkout.

No local or hosted GitHub Actions runner evidence verifies workflow parsing, action resolution, Node setup, cache behavior, or step-level failure propagation. DECISION-029 accepts the narrower negative-proof residual, but it does not supply execution evidence for this review.
The SHA-pinned actions/setup-node identity and its v7.0.0 annotation could not be independently verified without network access.

The candidate deliberately leaves stale pre-delivery statements in ROADMAP.md, project/milestones/M3.md, and docs/security-boundaries.md because those paths are outside ISSUE-0014’s allowed implementation scope; these remain documentation residuals for later governed reconciliation.
review.summary: BLOCKED. The workflow change itself is scoped and structurally matches the principal CI acceptance criteria, but project/status/CURRENT.md contains material contradictions about whether ISSUE-0014 started and whether frontend CI exists. Mandatory checks also could not be independently completed in the read-only, network-restricted sandbox, so repository rules prohibit a passing outcome. Residual risks include unverified GitHub Actions execution/action identity and intentionally stale delivery statements outside the issue’s allowed paths.
